paragraphs.en: Five hundred years ago, Nicolaus Copernicus proposed that the Earth might be one of several planets orbiting the Sun, rather than the centre of the universe. He compared the geocentric model to a monstrous form assembled from parts of different bodies, like the Creature Mary Shelley brought to life three centuries later in Frankenstein — each part appearing human on its own, but as a whole a grotesque patchwork.
paragraphs.zh: 五百年前，尼古拉·哥白尼提出，地球可能是环绕太阳运行的几颗行星之一，而非宇宙的中心。 他把地心说模型比作一个由不同身体的部件拼凑而成的怪物，就像玛丽·雪莱在三个世纪后的《弗兰肯斯坦》中赋予生命的那个造物——每个部分单独看都像人的模样，整体上却是一副怪诞的拼凑之物。

sents.en: Five hundred years ago, Nicolaus Copernicus proposed that the Earth might be one of several planets orbiting the Sun, rather than the centre of the universe.
sents.zh: 五百年前，尼古拉·哥白尼提出，地球可能是环绕太阳运行的几颗行星之一，而非宇宙的中心。

sents.en: He compared the geocentric model to a monstrous form assembled from parts of different bodies, like the Creature Mary Shelley brought to life three centuries later in Frankenstein — each part appearing human on its own, but as a whole a grotesque patchwork.
sents.zh: 他把地心说模型比作一个由不同身体的部件拼凑而成的怪物，就像玛丽·雪莱在三个世纪后的《弗兰肯斯坦》中赋予生命的那个造物——每个部分单独看都像人的模样，整体上却是一副怪诞的拼凑之物。

paragraphs.en: The geocentric model was built to directly match the sky: where a planet paused against the background stars and looped into retrograde, a dial was added so the planet would pause in its orbit around the Earth and loop backwards a while before resuming its normal course. In contrast, Copernicus recognised that the outer planets — Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn were known at the time — might enter retrograde loops due to parallax, their apparent positions shifting relative to the background stars as our orbit brings us near and then we pass them on our way around the Sun.
paragraphs.zh: 地心模型是为了直接匹配天空而构建的：在行星相对背景恒星停驻并绕出逆行圈的地方，就加装一个刻度盘，使行星在围绕地球的轨道上停顿下来，倒退一小段，然后恢复正常的行进路线。 相比之下，哥白尼认识到外行星——当时已知的是火星、木星和土星——可能因视差而进入逆行圈：随着我们的轨道使我们靠近它们，随后又在绕太阳运行的途中超过它们，它们的视位置会相对于背景恒星发生移动。

sents.en: The geocentric model was built to directly match the sky: where a planet paused against the background stars and looped into retrograde, a dial was added so the planet would pause in its orbit around the Earth and loop backwards a while before resuming its normal course.
sents.zh: 地心模型是为了直接匹配天空而构建的：在行星相对背景恒星停驻并绕出逆行圈的地方，就加装一个刻度盘，使行星在围绕地球的轨道上停顿下来，倒退一小段，然后恢复正常的行进路线。

sents.en: In contrast, Copernicus recognised that the outer planets — Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn were known at the time — might enter retrograde loops due to parallax, their apparent positions shifting relative to the background stars as our orbit brings us near and then we pass them on our way around the Sun.
sents.zh: 相比之下，哥白尼认识到外行星——当时已知的是火星、木星和土星——可能因视差而进入逆行圈：随着我们的轨道使我们靠近它们，随后又在绕太阳运行的途中超过它们，它们的视位置会相对于背景恒星发生移动。

paragraphs.en: Copernicus had no idea of the physics that Isaac Newton or Albert Einstein would eventually use to explain planetary motion. Nor did he imagine this motion resulted from the same phenomenon that causes apples to fall from trees, or paths of light to bend around the Sun. His model ended up with as many knobs and dials as the geocentric system due to his use of circles rather than ellipses to describe orbits.
paragraphs.zh: 哥白尼完全不知道，艾萨克·牛顿或阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦最终会利用怎样的物理学来解释行星运动。 他也没有想到，这种运动源于与苹果从树上落下、光线绕太阳弯曲相同的现象。 由于他使用圆形而非椭圆来描述轨道，他的模型最终拥有与地心说体系同样多的旋钮和刻度盘。

sents.en: Copernicus had no idea of the physics that Isaac Newton or Albert Einstein would eventually use to explain planetary motion.
sents.zh: 哥白尼完全不知道，艾萨克·牛顿或阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦最终会利用怎样的物理学来解释行星运动。

sents.en: Nor did he imagine this motion resulted from the same phenomenon that causes apples to fall from trees, or paths of light to bend around the Sun.
sents.zh: 他也没有想到，这种运动源于与苹果从树上落下、光线绕太阳弯曲相同的现象。

sents.en: His model ended up with as many knobs and dials as the geocentric system due to his use of circles rather than ellipses to describe orbits.
sents.zh: 由于他使用圆形而非椭圆来描述轨道，他的模型最终拥有与地心说体系同样多的旋钮和刻度盘。

paragraphs.en: Even so, Copernicus recognised that a Sun-centred theory afforded the possibility that it might eventually explain why phenomena like retrograde motion should appear as they do to us, despite the planets’ motion being continuously in one direction only. And in doing so, he paved the way for others like Newton and Einstein, who later fleshed out both the underlying concepts and formal mathematical descriptions of a solar system in which planetary motion is expected to appear with all the complexity we observe.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管如此，哥白尼认识到，以太阳为中心的理论提供了一种可能性，即它最终或许能解释为什么逆行等现象在我们看来是那样呈现的，尽管行星的运动始终只朝一个方向进行。 在这样做的同时，他为牛顿和爱因斯坦等后来者铺平了道路，这些人后来充实了太阳系的基本概念和形式化的数学描述，在这一体系中，行星运动被预期呈现出我们所观察到的一切复杂性。

sents.en: Even so, Copernicus recognised that a Sun-centred theory afforded the possibility that it might eventually explain why phenomena like retrograde motion should appear as they do to us, despite the planets’ motion being continuously in one direction only.
sents.zh: 尽管如此，哥白尼认识到，以太阳为中心的理论提供了一种可能性，即它最终或许能解释为什么逆行等现象在我们看来是那样呈现的，尽管行星的运动始终只朝一个方向进行。

sents.en: And in doing so, he paved the way for others like Newton and Einstein, who later fleshed out both the underlying concepts and formal mathematical descriptions of a solar system in which planetary motion is expected to appear with all the complexity we observe.
sents.zh: 在这样做的同时，他为牛顿和爱因斯坦等后来者铺平了道路，这些人后来充实了太阳系的基本概念和形式化的数学描述，在这一体系中，行星运动被预期呈现出我们所观察到的一切复杂性。

paragraphs.en: In hindsight, the discovery Copernicus’s proposal prompted was that broken symmetries — our off-centre perspective from a planet orbiting the Sun, and the non-uniform motions of all planets including ours — would complicate appearances within an ontological framework that is nonetheless simpler.
paragraphs.zh: 事后来看，哥白尼的提议所引发的发现是：被打破的对称性——我们位于一颗绕太阳运行的行星上的偏离中心的视角，以及包括我们自己在内所有行星的不均匀运动——会在一个本体论框架内使表象复杂化，尽管该框架本身更为简单。

paragraphs.en: In a similar sense, it may be argued that the standard cosmological model today — which gives an accurate description of phenomena but is nevertheless an amalgam of ad hoc patches, each inserted to unnaturally force the evolution of a universe that is otherwise expected to be different from the way it appears — bears a closer resemblance to Frankenstein’s monster than it does the simple explanations of planetary motion given by Newton and Einstein. For despite all the dials and knobs that have been added to ensure the standard model does directly resemble appearances, after a century of development it still affords no explanation of why our universe should be expected to expand , as it appears to do.
paragraphs.zh: 从类似的意义上说，可以认为今天的标准宇宙学模型——它虽然能准确描述现象，却是一堆特设补丁的拼凑物，每一个补丁都是为了不自然地强行让宇宙的演化符合观测而插入的，否则宇宙本应呈现出与实际不同的样子——与其说像牛顿和爱因斯坦对行星运动给出的简洁解释，不如说更像弗兰肯斯坦的怪物。 因为尽管为了让标准模型直接符合表象而添加了各种旋钮和调节参数，经过一个世纪的发展，它仍然无法解释为什么我们的宇宙理应会膨胀，尽管它看起来确实在膨胀。

sents.en: For despite all the dials and knobs that have been added to ensure the standard model does directly resemble appearances, after a century of development it still affords no explanation of why our universe should be expected to expand , as it appears to do.
sents.zh: 因为尽管为了让标准模型直接符合表象而添加了各种旋钮和调节参数，经过一个世纪的发展，它仍然无法解释为什么我们的宇宙理应会膨胀，尽管它看起来确实在膨胀。

paragraphs.en: In the Copernican tradition, we ought to ask why our universe should expand. The standard cosmological model affords no such explanation. It is based on a principle, famously promoted by Einstein together with his colleague Willem de Sitter, that characterises the universe as expanding in spite of a tendency to decelerate because it is filled with everything we see . This is important: according to the basic Einstein-de Sitter framework for describing cosmic expansion, all the galaxies and light we see across the universe are thought to work against the universe’s expansion, slowing it down; and anything driving expansion is an ad hoc dial we’ve added so that the base model fits appearances better than it naturally should.
paragraphs.zh: 在哥白尼传统中，我们应当追问：为什么我们的宇宙会膨胀。 标准宇宙学模型并未提供这样的解释。 该模型基于一个原理——由爱因斯坦与其同事威廉·德西特著名地倡导——将宇宙刻画为正在膨胀，尽管宇宙因充满我们所见的一切而存在减速的趋势。 这一点很重要：根据描述宇宙膨胀的基本爱因斯坦-德西特框架，我们在宇宙中看到的所有星系和光都被认为在对抗宇宙的膨胀，使其减速；而任何驱动膨胀的因素都是我们额外添加的临时旋钮，目的是让基础模型比其自然状态更符合表象。

sents.en: In the Copernican tradition, we ought to ask why our universe should expand.
sents.zh: 在哥白尼传统中，我们应当追问：为什么我们的宇宙会膨胀。

sents.en: The standard cosmological model affords no such explanation.
sents.zh: 标准宇宙学模型并未提供这样的解释。

sents.en: It is based on a principle, famously promoted by Einstein together with his colleague Willem de Sitter, that characterises the universe as expanding in spite of a tendency to decelerate because it is filled with everything we see .
sents.zh: 该模型基于一个原理——由爱因斯坦与其同事威廉·德西特著名地倡导——将宇宙刻画为正在膨胀，尽管宇宙因充满我们所见的一切而存在减速的趋势。

sents.en: This is important: according to the basic Einstein-de Sitter framework for describing cosmic expansion, all the galaxies and light we see across the universe are thought to work against the universe’s expansion, slowing it down; and anything driving expansion is an ad hoc dial we’ve added so that the base model fits appearances better than it naturally should.
sents.zh: 这一点很重要：根据描述宇宙膨胀的基本爱因斯坦-德西特框架，我们在宇宙中看到的所有星系和光都被认为在对抗宇宙的膨胀，使其减速；而任何驱动膨胀的因素都是我们额外添加的临时旋钮，目的是让基础模型比其自然状态更符合表象。

paragraphs.en: In fact, this tendency for light and matter to slow cosmic expansion mathematically blows up to an infinite amount at the Big Bang. Therefore, the model’s only “explanation” for why our universe even could be expanding today is that it began with such a tremendous rate that momentum carried it against its natural tendency towards the opposite. For this reason, a century ago British astronomer Arthur Stanley Eddington complained of the Einstein-de Sitter model that would dominate twentieth century cosmology, “One cannot deny the possibility, but it is difficult to see what mental satisfaction such a theory is supposed to afford.”
paragraphs.zh: 事实上，光和物质减缓宇宙膨胀的这一趋势在数学上会在大爆炸时爆炸成一个无穷大的量。 因此，该模型对我们宇宙如今竟能够膨胀的唯一“解释”是，它以一种极其巨大的速率开始，靠动量逆着它趋向相反方向的自然趋势而运动。 正因如此，一个世纪前，英国天文学家亚瑟·斯坦利·爱丁顿对那个将主导二十世纪宇宙学的爱因斯坦-德西特模型抱怨道：“人们无法否认这种可能性，但很难看出这样一个理论究竟能带来什么精神上的满足。”

sents.en: In fact, this tendency for light and matter to slow cosmic expansion mathematically blows up to an infinite amount at the Big Bang.
sents.zh: 事实上，光和物质减缓宇宙膨胀的这一趋势在数学上会在大爆炸时爆炸成一个无穷大的量。

sents.en: Therefore, the model’s only “explanation” for why our universe even could be expanding today is that it began with such a tremendous rate that momentum carried it against its natural tendency towards the opposite.
sents.zh: 因此，该模型对我们宇宙如今竟能够膨胀的唯一“解释”是，它以一种极其巨大的速率开始，靠动量逆着它趋向相反方向的自然趋势而运动。

sents.en: For this reason, a century ago British astronomer Arthur Stanley Eddington complained of the Einstein-de Sitter model that would dominate twentieth century cosmology, “One cannot deny the possibility, but it is difficult to see what mental satisfaction such a theory is supposed to afford.”
sents.zh: 正因如此，一个世纪前，英国天文学家亚瑟·斯坦利·爱丁顿对那个将主导二十世纪宇宙学的爱因斯坦-德西特模型抱怨道：“人们无法否认这种可能性，但很难看出这样一个理论究竟能带来什么精神上的满足。”

paragraphs.en: Much like its Ptolemaic predecessor, this model has since been augmented with various features allowing it to fit the data with impressive accuracy. First, there is an inflationary epoch, thought to have occurred a moment after the Big Bang, which would drive a fleeting period of exponential expansion and erase several tensions the Einstein-de Sitter model otherwise leaves unresolved — though leaving the initial expansion problem untouched. Then for a long while the universe is thought to have decelerated, its slowing rate driven primarily by radiation in the early universe followed later by matter, in good alignment with Einstein-de Sitter. Finally, after several billion years a component we’ve come to call dark energy, which does tend to drive expansion, is thought to have become significant enough that the expansion rate eventually began to accelerate.
paragraphs.zh: 与其托勒密式的前身非常相似，这个模型后来也被加入了各种特性，使其能够以惊人的精度拟合数据。 首先，存在一个暴胀时期，被认为发生在大爆炸后的一瞬间，它会驱动一个短暂的指数膨胀阶段，并消除爱因斯坦-德西特模型原本遗留的若干矛盾——尽管并未触及初始膨胀问题。 然后，在很长一段时间里，宇宙被认为处于减速状态，其减速速率在早期宇宙中主要由辐射主导，随后由物质主导，这与爱因斯坦-德西特模型相当吻合。 最终，在数十亿年之后，一种我们如今称之为暗能量的成分——它确实倾向于驱动膨胀——被认为变得足够显著，以至于膨胀速率最终开始加快。

sents.en: Much like its Ptolemaic predecessor, this model has since been augmented with various features allowing it to fit the data with impressive accuracy.
sents.zh: 与其托勒密式的前身非常相似，这个模型后来也被加入了各种特性，使其能够以惊人的精度拟合数据。

sents.en: Finally, after several billion years a component we’ve come to call dark energy, which does tend to drive expansion, is thought to have become significant enough that the expansion rate eventually began to accelerate.
sents.zh: 最终，在数十亿年之后，一种我们如今称之为暗能量的成分——它确实倾向于驱动膨胀——被认为变得足够显著，以至于膨胀速率最终开始加快。

paragraphs.en: In comparison with the Ptolemaic model, both inflation and dark energy are similar to the eccentric and equant: later patches, added to a universe filled with the stuff we observe directly, that enables us to describe the universe we see in spite of the fact that without these patches the more basic physics suggests the universe should not evolve as it appears to do.
paragraphs.zh: 与托勒密模型相比，暴胀和暗能量都类似于偏心圆和均衡点：它们是后来添加的补丁，加在一个充满我们直接观测到的物质的宇宙之上，使我们能够描述我们所看到的宇宙，尽管若没有这些补丁，更基础的物理学表明宇宙本不应像它表面那样演化。

paragraphs.en: A bare Einstein-de Sitter universe should not appear the same in different regions of the sky that could not have interacted before the times we now see, due to the finite speed of light. And such a universe should not appear spatially flat, as ours appears to be. Inflation is the dial we use to fix both of these problems.
paragraphs.zh: 由于光速有限，一个纯粹的爱因斯坦-德西特宇宙在天空的不同区域本不应当呈现出相同的样子，因为这些区域在我们如今所见的时刻之前不可能发生过相互作用。 而且这样的宇宙在空间上也不应当是平坦的，而我们的宇宙看起来却是平坦的。 暴胀正是我们用来同时解决这两个问题的手段。

sents.en: A bare Einstein-de Sitter universe should not appear the same in different regions of the sky that could not have interacted before the times we now see, due to the finite speed of light.
sents.zh: 由于光速有限，一个纯粹的爱因斯坦-德西特宇宙在天空的不同区域本不应当呈现出相同的样子，因为这些区域在我们如今所见的时刻之前不可能发生过相互作用。

sents.en: And such a universe should not appear spatially flat, as ours appears to be.
sents.zh: 而且这样的宇宙在空间上也不应当是平坦的，而我们的宇宙看起来却是平坦的。

sents.en: Inflation is the dial we use to fix both of these problems.
sents.zh: 暴胀正是我们用来同时解决这两个问题的手段。

paragraphs.en: An Einstein-de Sitter universe also should never come to expand at an accelerating rate as we’ve observed — let alone expand to start with. Dark energy fixes the former issue, but its effect is null at the Big Bang and only gradually becomes significant over billions of years, so it cannot explain why the universe should ever have expanded in the beginning. And inflation can only happen within an already existing, expanding universe — so invoking it as the primary cause would be tautology.
paragraphs.zh: 一个爱因斯坦-德西特宇宙同样绝不应该像我们所观测到的那样加速膨胀——更不用说从一开始就在膨胀了。 暗能量解决了前一个问题，但它的效应在大爆炸时为零，而且要经过数十亿年才逐渐变得显著，因此它无法解释宇宙为何在一开始就发生了膨胀。 而暴胀只能发生在一个已经存在、正在膨胀的宇宙之中——所以把它作为首要原因来援引无异于同义反复。

sents.en: An Einstein-de Sitter universe also should never come to expand at an accelerating rate as we’ve observed — let alone expand to start with.
sents.zh: 一个爱因斯坦-德西特宇宙同样绝不应该像我们所观测到的那样加速膨胀——更不用说从一开始就在膨胀了。

sents.en: Dark energy fixes the former issue, but its effect is null at the Big Bang and only gradually becomes significant over billions of years, so it cannot explain why the universe should ever have expanded in the beginning.
sents.zh: 暗能量解决了前一个问题，但它的效应在大爆炸时为零，而且要经过数十亿年才逐渐变得显著，因此它无法解释宇宙为何在一开始就发生了膨胀。

sents.en: And inflation can only happen within an already existing, expanding universe — so invoking it as the primary cause would be tautology.
sents.zh: 而暴胀只能发生在一个已经存在、正在膨胀的宇宙之中——所以把它作为首要原因来援引无异于同义反复。

paragraphs.en: More recently, the dark energy patch has started to need patches of its own. Large surveys of galaxy clustering and supernovae have been read as favouring a dark energy that weakens over time rather than holding steady, and astronomers have proposed evolving dark energy models — adding an evolution dial to a source of repulsion that was never explained in the first place. Meanwhile the expansion rate measured locally, from nearby stars and supernovae, has stubbornly refused to agree with the rate inferred from the early universe, and that disagreement too has drawn a growing list of proposed fixes, each one another dial.
paragraphs.zh: 更近一些时候，暗能量这块补丁也开始需要打补丁了。 对星系成团性和超新星的大规模巡天被解读为更倾向于一种随时间减弱而非保持恒定的暗能量，天文学家由此提出了演化的暗能量模型——在一个本就从未得到解释的排斥之源上，又加装了一个演化旋钮。 与此同时，通过近距恒星和超新星在本地测得的膨胀率，始终顽固地不肯与从早期宇宙推断出的膨胀率相一致，而这一分歧同样催生了一份越来越长的拟议修正清单，每一项都是又一个旋钮。

sents.en: More recently, the dark energy patch has started to need patches of its own.
sents.zh: 更近一些时候，暗能量这块补丁也开始需要打补丁了。

sents.en: Large surveys of galaxy clustering and supernovae have been read as favouring a dark energy that weakens over time rather than holding steady, and astronomers have proposed evolving dark energy models — adding an evolution dial to a source of repulsion that was never explained in the first place.
sents.zh: 对星系成团性和超新星的大规模巡天被解读为更倾向于一种随时间减弱而非保持恒定的暗能量，天文学家由此提出了演化的暗能量模型——在一个本就从未得到解释的排斥之源上，又加装了一个演化旋钮。

sents.en: Meanwhile the expansion rate measured locally, from nearby stars and supernovae, has stubbornly refused to agree with the rate inferred from the early universe, and that disagreement too has drawn a growing list of proposed fixes, each one another dial.
sents.zh: 与此同时，通过近距恒星和超新星在本地测得的膨胀率，始终顽固地不肯与从早期宇宙推断出的膨胀率相一致，而这一分歧同样催生了一份越来越长的拟议修正清单，每一项都是又一个旋钮。

paragraphs.en: When an ad hoc patch starts needing ad hoc patches of its own, in a model that fundamentally abhors the very phenomenon it was built to describe, that should be a strong sign the trouble lies in the base model.
paragraphs.zh: 当一种临时补丁开始需要自己的临时补丁时，而在一个从根本上憎恶它所要描述的现象本身的模型中，这应当是一个强烈的信号，表明问题出在基础模型上。

paragraphs.en: In light of the problems the standard cosmological model has with reconciling the evidence and providing an explanation for the world we seem to live in — the growing number of knobs and dials to recover a phenomenologically accurate description of a universe that is nonetheless fundamentally expected to be different — we ought to take a page from Copernicus and ask what symmetries we may be assuming are fundamental, which our reality may in fact essentially break. We should ask what appearances we see that may not directly represent the world that is, but which may instead only appear as such because our place in the universe is not central, so our perspective is owed in part to a broken symmetry.
paragraphs.zh: 鉴于标准宇宙学模型在调和证据并为我们似乎居住的世界提供解释方面所面临的问题——为了对一个宇宙恢复唯象上准确的描述，需要越来越多的旋钮和刻度盘，而这个宇宙从根本上却被期望与我们的描述有所不同——我们应当借鉴哥白尼的做法，追问我们可能假定了哪些基本对称性，而我们的现实实际上可能从根本上破坏了这些对称性。 我们应当追问，我们所看到的那些表象，可能并不直接代表真实存在的世界，而之所以呈现为如此表象，或许只是因为我们在宇宙中的位置并非中心，因此我们的视角在部分上源于一种破缺的对称性。

sents.en: In light of the problems the standard cosmological model has with reconciling the evidence and providing an explanation for the world we seem to live in — the growing number of knobs and dials to recover a phenomenologically accurate description of a universe that is nonetheless fundamentally expected to be different — we ought to take a page from Copernicus and ask what symmetries we may be assuming are fundamental, which our reality may in fact essentially break.
sents.zh: 鉴于标准宇宙学模型在调和证据并为我们似乎居住的世界提供解释方面所面临的问题——为了对一个宇宙恢复唯象上准确的描述，需要越来越多的旋钮和刻度盘，而这个宇宙从根本上却被期望与我们的描述有所不同——我们应当借鉴哥白尼的做法，追问我们可能假定了哪些基本对称性，而我们的现实实际上可能从根本上破坏了这些对称性。

sents.en: We should ask what appearances we see that may not directly represent the world that is, but which may instead only appear as such because our place in the universe is not central, so our perspective is owed in part to a broken symmetry.
sents.zh: 我们应当追问，我们所看到的那些表象，可能并不直接代表真实存在的世界，而之所以呈现为如此表象，或许只是因为我们在宇宙中的位置并非中心，因此我们的视角在部分上源于一种破缺的对称性。

paragraphs.en: This is not idle speculation. In essence, physics is an exercise in recognising the various forms in which symmetries are broken in nature. By this, I mean generally any phenomenon that removes a degree of symmetry within the natural world.
paragraphs.zh: 这并非无端的猜测。 从本质上讲，物理学就是一项辨认自然界中各种对称性破缺形式的活动。 我所说的对称性破缺，泛指自然界中任何消除某种对称自由度的现象。

sents.en: This is not idle speculation.
sents.zh: 这并非无端的猜测。

sents.en: In essence, physics is an exercise in recognising the various forms in which symmetries are broken in nature.
sents.zh: 从本质上讲，物理学就是一项辨认自然界中各种对称性破缺形式的活动。

sents.en: By this, I mean generally any phenomenon that removes a degree of symmetry within the natural world.
sents.zh: 我所说的对称性破缺，泛指自然界中任何消除某种对称自由度的现象。

paragraphs.en: For example, because the Sun spins, it is wider around its equator. The Sun breaks one dimension of symmetry by spinning around an axis, and causes an equatorial bulge we can measure. And by measuring the Sun’s rotational rate and the size of its equatorial bulge, we can estimate other physical properties that are more difficult to measure, like its density profile.
paragraphs.zh: 例如，由于太阳会自转，它在赤道附近更宽。 太阳通过绕轴自转打破了一个维度的对称性，并造成了我们可以测量到的赤道隆起。 通过测量太阳的自转速率和赤道隆起的大小，我们可以估算出其他更难测量的物理性质，比如它的密度分布。

sents.en: For example, because the Sun spins, it is wider around its equator.
sents.zh: 例如，由于太阳会自转，它在赤道附近更宽。

sents.en: The Sun breaks one dimension of symmetry by spinning around an axis, and causes an equatorial bulge we can measure.
sents.zh: 太阳通过绕轴自转打破了一个维度的对称性，并造成了我们可以测量到的赤道隆起。

sents.en: And by measuring the Sun’s rotational rate and the size of its equatorial bulge, we can estimate other physical properties that are more difficult to measure, like its density profile.
sents.zh: 通过测量太阳的自转速率和赤道隆起的大小，我们可以估算出其他更难测量的物理性质，比如它的密度分布。

paragraphs.en: Or imagine that the Earth was at the centre of everything, and we were orbited only by the Sun which moved in a perfect circle around us, and that the sky was perfectly uniform with no randomly scattered stars across it. In this case, the only broken symmetry we could reference in our sky would be the Sun itself. We would still have day and night. The sky would still be brighter as we look closer to the Sun. In this case, we could build a model to describe the Sun as orbiting the Earth once a day, at a fixed distance from Earth.
paragraphs.zh: 或者想象一下，地球处于一切的中心，只有太阳围绕我们运行，它沿着完美的圆形绕我们转动，而天空完全均匀，没有随机散布的星星。 在这种情况下，我们在天空中唯一能参照的破缺对称就只有太阳本身。 我们仍然会有白天和黑夜。 越靠近太阳的方向看去，天空仍然会更明亮。 在这种情况下，我们可以建立一个模型，把太阳描述为每天绕地球运行一圈，且与地球保持固定的距离。

sents.en: Or imagine that the Earth was at the centre of everything, and we were orbited only by the Sun which moved in a perfect circle around us, and that the sky was perfectly uniform with no randomly scattered stars across it.
sents.zh: 或者想象一下，地球处于一切的中心，只有太阳围绕我们运行，它沿着完美的圆形绕我们转动，而天空完全均匀，没有随机散布的星星。

sents.en: In this case, the only broken symmetry we could reference in our sky would be the Sun itself.
sents.zh: 在这种情况下，我们在天空中唯一能参照的破缺对称就只有太阳本身。

sents.en: We would still have day and night.
sents.zh: 我们仍然会有白天和黑夜。

sents.en: The sky would still be brighter as we look closer to the Sun.
sents.zh: 越靠近太阳的方向看去，天空仍然会更明亮。

sents.en: In this case, we could build a model to describe the Sun as orbiting the Earth once a day, at a fixed distance from Earth.
sents.zh: 在这种情况下，我们可以建立一个模型，把太阳描述为每天绕地球运行一圈，且与地球保持固定的距离。

paragraphs.en: But with no other symmetry breaking to worry about, we could equivalently describe the Earth as spinning around once a day while the Sun remains fixed in place. In fact, if all else were the same but it was really the Earth orbiting a fixed Sun, still in a perfect circle, we could not tell the difference from the moving Sun picture. Due to unbroken symmetry, either description could be used regardless of what is really going on.
paragraphs.zh: 但由于没有其他需要担心的对称性破缺，我们同样可以把地球描述为每天自转一周，而太阳保持固定不动。 事实上，如果其他条件都相同，而真的是地球在绕一个固定的太阳运转，且轨道仍是完美的圆形，那么我们无法从太阳运动的图像中分辨出差别。 由于对称性未被打破，无论实际情况如何，这两种描述都可以使用。

sents.en: But with no other symmetry breaking to worry about, we could equivalently describe the Earth as spinning around once a day while the Sun remains fixed in place.
sents.zh: 但由于没有其他需要担心的对称性破缺，我们同样可以把地球描述为每天自转一周，而太阳保持固定不动。

sents.en: In fact, if all else were the same but it was really the Earth orbiting a fixed Sun, still in a perfect circle, we could not tell the difference from the moving Sun picture.
sents.zh: 事实上，如果其他条件都相同，而真的是地球在绕一个固定的太阳运转，且轨道仍是完美的圆形，那么我们无法从太阳运动的图像中分辨出差别。

sents.en: Due to unbroken symmetry, either description could be used regardless of what is really going on.
sents.zh: 由于对称性未被打破，无论实际情况如何，这两种描述都可以使用。

paragraphs.en: But now consider our reality. Since the Earth follows an elliptical orbit rather than a circular one, careful measurements show that the Sun grows and shrinks in the course of a year. The model that describes the Sun as orbiting around the Earth once a day has no mechanism for the apparent growing and shrinking of the Sun annually, so we would have to add another dial that makes it move outward for six months, then in, as well as orbiting once a day. In contrast, an elliptical orbit of a spinning Earth has the same effect. Each model here has two dials to represent two broken symmetries.
paragraphs.zh: 但现在来看看我们的现实情况。 由于地球沿椭圆轨道而非圆形轨道运行，精确的测量表明太阳在一年之中会变大和变小。 把太阳描述为每天绕地球一圈的模型没有任何机制能解释太阳每年明显的大小变化，因此我们不得不增加另一个转盘，使它在六个月里向外移动，然后再向内移动，同时每天仍绕行一圈。 相比之下，自转地球的椭圆轨道则具有同样的效果。 这里的每个模型都有两个转盘来表示两种被打破的对称性。

sents.en: But now consider our reality.
sents.zh: 但现在来看看我们的现实情况。

sents.en: Since the Earth follows an elliptical orbit rather than a circular one, careful measurements show that the Sun grows and shrinks in the course of a year.
sents.zh: 由于地球沿椭圆轨道而非圆形轨道运行，精确的测量表明太阳在一年之中会变大和变小。

sents.en: The model that describes the Sun as orbiting around the Earth once a day has no mechanism for the apparent growing and shrinking of the Sun annually, so we would have to add another dial that makes it move outward for six months, then in, as well as orbiting once a day.
sents.zh: 把太阳描述为每天绕地球一圈的模型没有任何机制能解释太阳每年明显的大小变化，因此我们不得不增加另一个转盘，使它在六个月里向外移动，然后再向内移动，同时每天仍绕行一圈。

sents.en: In contrast, an elliptical orbit of a spinning Earth has the same effect.
sents.zh: 相比之下，自转地球的椭圆轨道则具有同样的效果。

sents.en: Each model here has two dials to represent two broken symmetries.
sents.zh: 这里的每个模型都有两个转盘来表示两种被打破的对称性。

paragraphs.en: But then, because the sky is filled with recognisable patterns, the Sun not only appears to grow and shrink, but also appears to follow a circular path against the background stars as it grows and shrinks. Now, if we want to use the geocentric model we need a third dial to spin the stars around at a rate that matches the Sun’s daily rotation almost exactly, but which is mismatched by about a degree per day so that in 365.25 days (per year) the Sun appears to follow a 360-degree circular path against the background stars.
paragraphs.zh: 但接下来，因为天空中布满了可识别的图案，太阳不仅看起来会变大和变小，而且在变大变小的同时，看起来还会相对于背景恒星沿一条圆形路径运动。 现在，如果我们想使用地心模型，就需要第三个表盘，让恒星以与太阳每日自转几乎完全一致的速度旋转，但每日约有偏离一度的差异，这样在365.25天（一年）里，太阳看起来就相对于背景恒星沿一条360度的圆形路径运动。

sents.en: But then, because the sky is filled with recognisable patterns, the Sun not only appears to grow and shrink, but also appears to follow a circular path against the background stars as it grows and shrinks.
sents.zh: 但接下来，因为天空中布满了可识别的图案，太阳不仅看起来会变大和变小，而且在变大变小的同时，看起来还会相对于背景恒星沿一条圆形路径运动。

sents.en: Now, if we want to use the geocentric model we need a third dial to spin the stars around at a rate that matches the Sun’s daily rotation almost exactly, but which is mismatched by about a degree per day so that in 365.25 days (per year) the Sun appears to follow a 360-degree circular path against the background stars.
sents.zh: 现在，如果我们想使用地心模型，就需要第三个表盘，让恒星以与太阳每日自转几乎完全一致的速度旋转，但每日约有偏离一度的差异，这样在365.25天（一年）里，太阳看起来就相对于背景恒星沿一条360度的圆形路径运动。

paragraphs.en: In contrast, the Sun-centred model with fixed stars and Earth both spinning daily and orbiting the Sun on an elliptical path needs no extra dial to capture the Sun’s apparent annual orbit, as measured from Earth, with respect to those background stars. It’s already baked in, so the Sun-centred model achieves the same with two dials as the Earth-centred model achieves with three.
paragraphs.zh: 相比之下，在太阳中心的模型中，恒星与地球都每日自转，且地球沿椭圆轨道绕太阳公转，因此无需额外的刻度盘就能刻画从地球上测得的太阳相对于那些背景恒星的表观周年运动。 这已经内置其中，因此太阳中心的模型用两个刻度盘就实现了地球中心模型用三个刻度盘才能达到的效果。

sents.en: In contrast, the Sun-centred model with fixed stars and Earth both spinning daily and orbiting the Sun on an elliptical path needs no extra dial to capture the Sun’s apparent annual orbit, as measured from Earth, with respect to those background stars.
sents.zh: 相比之下，在太阳中心的模型中，恒星与地球都每日自转，且地球沿椭圆轨道绕太阳公转，因此无需额外的刻度盘就能刻画从地球上测得的太阳相对于那些背景恒星的表观周年运动。

sents.en: It’s already baked in, so the Sun-centred model achieves the same with two dials as the Earth-centred model achieves with three.
sents.zh: 这已经内置其中，因此太阳中心的模型用两个刻度盘就实现了地球中心模型用三个刻度盘才能达到的效果。

paragraphs.en: Adding in the planets with their retrograde loops, we find more of the same and the geocentric model’s count of extra dials grows and grows, while the broken symmetry of our own off-centre position in the Sun-centred model relative to our Earth-centred observing platform continues to do the work of reconciling the apparent phenomena with a minimal set of dials.
paragraphs.zh: 把行星及其逆行环圈加进来后，我们发现情况如出一辙：地心模型中额外的刻度盘数量不断增长，而在以太阳为中心的模型中，我们自身相对于以地球为中心的观测平台所处的偏离中心位置所带来的对称性破缺，继续发挥着作用，以最少的一组刻度盘调和各种表观现象。

paragraphs.en: And Copernicus’s great contribution, as noted above, was in recognising that the Sun-centred model had the capacity to achieve with fewer dials what the geocentric model required in abundance. He did not figure out the actual dials and the physical framework needed to do the work: all of that was found over the next century, by people like Thomas Digges, Johannes Kepler, and Galileo Galilei, who recognised Copernicus’s push for logical parsimony as a mark in favour of his proposal. And the physical context and minimal set of dials they developed was eventually explained by Newton, who formulated a single law (of universal gravitation) that accounted for all of it, as well as the tides and the fact that apples fall from trees.
paragraphs.zh: 如上所述，哥白尼的伟大贡献在于认识到，以太阳为中心的模型能够用更少的刻度盘实现地心模型需要大量刻度盘才能完成的工作。 他并没有弄清完成这项工作所需的实际刻度盘和物理框架：这一切是在之后的一个世纪里被发现的，由托马斯·迪格斯、约翰内斯·开普勒和伽利略·伽利莱等人完成，他们认识到哥白尼对逻辑简洁性的追求是其学说的一大优势。 而他们发展出的物理背景和最小刻度盘集合最终由牛顿解释清楚，他提出了单一的定律（万有引力定律），解释了这一切，以及潮汐现象和苹果会从树上掉落的事实。

sents.en: And Copernicus’s great contribution, as noted above, was in recognising that the Sun-centred model had the capacity to achieve with fewer dials what the geocentric model required in abundance.
sents.zh: 如上所述，哥白尼的伟大贡献在于认识到，以太阳为中心的模型能够用更少的刻度盘实现地心模型需要大量刻度盘才能完成的工作。

sents.en: He did not figure out the actual dials and the physical framework needed to do the work: all of that was found over the next century, by people like Thomas Digges, Johannes Kepler, and Galileo Galilei, who recognised Copernicus’s push for logical parsimony as a mark in favour of his proposal.
sents.zh: 他并没有弄清完成这项工作所需的实际刻度盘和物理框架：这一切是在之后的一个世纪里被发现的，由托马斯·迪格斯、约翰内斯·开普勒和伽利略·伽利莱等人完成，他们认识到哥白尼对逻辑简洁性的追求是其学说的一大优势。

sents.en: And the physical context and minimal set of dials they developed was eventually explained by Newton, who formulated a single law (of universal gravitation) that accounted for all of it, as well as the tides and the fact that apples fall from trees.
sents.zh: 而他们发展出的物理背景和最小刻度盘集合最终由牛顿解释清楚，他提出了单一的定律（万有引力定律），解释了这一切，以及潮汐现象和苹果会从树上掉落的事实。

paragraphs.en: It is no exaggeration to say that if we did not live in a solar system with several other planets as well as our own, all following elliptical paths around the Sun, we would not have worked out what gravitation is. It was the hard problem of working out the minimal set of broken symmetries that cause apparent planetary retrograde loops to occur, which took thousands of years and significant wrong turns and ingenuity along the way, that produced Newtonian physics.
paragraphs.zh: 可以毫不夸张地说，如果我们不是生活在这样一个太阳系中——除了我们自己的行星之外还有其他几颗行星，它们都沿着椭圆轨道绕太阳运行——我们就不会弄清楚引力究竟是什么。 正是找出导致行星视逆行圈出现的最小破缺对称集合这一难题，耗费了数千年时间，其间经历了重大的弯折与巧思，最终催生了牛顿物理学。

sents.en: It is no exaggeration to say that if we did not live in a solar system with several other planets as well as our own, all following elliptical paths around the Sun, we would not have worked out what gravitation is.
sents.zh: 可以毫不夸张地说，如果我们不是生活在这样一个太阳系中——除了我们自己的行星之外还有其他几颗行星，它们都沿着椭圆轨道绕太阳运行——我们就不会弄清楚引力究竟是什么。

sents.en: It was the hard problem of working out the minimal set of broken symmetries that cause apparent planetary retrograde loops to occur, which took thousands of years and significant wrong turns and ingenuity along the way, that produced Newtonian physics.
sents.zh: 正是找出导致行星视逆行圈出现的最小破缺对称集合这一难题，耗费了数千年时间，其间经历了重大的弯折与巧思，最终催生了牛顿物理学。

paragraphs.en: Therefore, it was by taking the problem of explanation seriously — by caring enough to sort out the actual cause of the phenomena and the minimal set of dials (i.e. spinning planets following elliptical orbits around the Sun) and associated broken symmetries that would explain the world we observe — that Copernicus spearheaded the Scientific Revolution.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，正是通过认真对待解释问题——通过足够在意地梳理出现象的实际原因，以及能够解释我们所观察到的世界的最小一组旋钮（即围绕太阳沿椭圆轨道运行的行星）和相关的破缺对称性——哥白尼才引领了科学革命。

paragraphs.en: In 2009, I decided to work on the problem that the standard cosmological model fails to explain why the universe should expand for my PhD. New evidence for dark energy in the form of a cosmological constant had been discovered just a decade earlier, and I was bothered by the same failure to fundamentally explain cosmic expansion that had perturbed Eddington: while the model does provide an accurate description, I find no mental satisfaction due to its failure to explain why the universe should ever have expanded at all. I think this lack of explanation is the most significant failing in physics, as well as the most underappreciated problem of the past century. Therefore, after a year of beating my head against a problem I found increasingly uninteresting, I decided if I was going to continue studying physics this was where I wanted to put my effort.

paragraphs.en: I took as my starting point the fact that the standard model, in addition to a few seemingly reasonable and empirically motivated assumptions, contains a significant assumption that the universe’s clock is the same one carried by an average galaxy. You see: according to Einstein’s theories of relativity, everything in the universe has its own personal clock, and times are measured differently when objects move relative to one another. The assumption that galaxies should on average carry the same personal clock as the universe is equivalent to assuming the matter in our universe is, on average, not moving.
paragraphs.zh: 我以如下事实作为出发点：标准模型除了包含一些看似合理且有经验依据的假设之外，还包含一个重要的假设，即宇宙的时钟与一个平均星系所携带的时钟是同一个。 你要知道：根据爱因斯坦的相对论，宇宙中的每样东西都有自己专属的时钟，当物体彼此相对运动时，时间的测量结果会有所不同。 假设星系平均而言携带与宇宙相同的专属时钟，就等价于假设我们宇宙中的物质平均而言是不运动的。

paragraphs.en: We call this frame of reference comoving in cosmology, and use it to describe the bulk motion of galaxies which all have some motion relative to it due to local gravitational interactions with their neighbours. And we take the bundle of worldlines that describe the passage of time measured on comoving clocks to be at rest, and therefore in a relativistic sense to essentially define what space at any given cosmic moment is.
paragraphs.zh: 在宇宙学中我们把这个参考系称为共动参考系，并用它来描述星系的整体运动——由于与邻近天体发生局部引力相互作用，星系相对于该参考系都有一些运动。 我们把描述由共动时钟所测时间的那些世界线束视为静止的，因此在相对论意义上，它们基本上定义了任一给定宇宙时刻的空间是什么。

sents.zh: 我们把描述由共动时钟所测时间的那些世界线束视为静止的，因此在相对论意义上，它们基本上定义了任一给定宇宙时刻的空间是什么。

paragraphs.en: This definition is a somewhat thinly disguised version of the geocentric principle that put the Earth at the centre of motion within our solar system and described the Sun as orbiting around us. Only in cosmology we assume it’s matter-on-the-whole that sets what it means for matter to be at-rest.
paragraphs.zh: 这一定义在某种程度上是地心说原则的一个较为露骨的翻版，该原则将地球置于太阳系运动的中心，并认为太阳围绕我们运转。 只有在宇宙学中，我们才假定是作为整体的物质规定了物质处于静止的含义。

In fact, it could even be that such inertia is what gives matter its mass. These were some early speculations I had that I think turn out to have been rather on-the-nose.
paragraphs.zh: 这个假设并不算太糟糕，但它终究只是一个假设，也有可能物质在宇宙中其实具有某种不可忽视的体惯性。 事实上，甚至有可能是这种惯性赋予了物质质量。 这些是我早年的一些推测，如今看来它们可以说相当切中要害。

sents.en: This isn’t a terrible assumption to make; but still, it is an assumption, and it could be instead that matter has some nontrivial bulk inertia through the universe.
sents.zh: 这个假设并不算太糟糕，但它终究只是一个假设，也有可能物质在宇宙中其实具有某种不可忽视的体惯性。

sents.zh: 这些是我早年的一些推测，如今看来它们可以说相当切中要害。

paragraphs.en: It is no accident that this assumption about matter being on average essentially at rest is deeply embedded in standard cosmology. When Einstein developed general relativity, he was strongly influenced by the writings of Austrian physicist and philosopher Ernst Mach, and on Mach’s principle he believed that inertia itself should be determined by the matter distribution of the universe as a whole. A body’s resistance to acceleration shouldn’t be a brute fact about space, he thought; it should be something the rest of the matter in the universe confers on it. So when Einstein wrote down the first relativistic cosmology in 1917, he built it around a universal “world-matter” — a smooth distribution filling the universe, at rest with respect to itself, which would supply the standard every motion is measured against.
paragraphs.zh: 关于物质平均而言基本上处于静止这一假设深深植根于标准宇宙学之中，这绝非偶然。 当爱因斯坦发展广义相对论时，他深受奥地利物理学家兼哲学家恩斯特·马赫著作的影响，并且基于马赫的原理，他认为惯性本身应当由作为整体的宇宙的物质分布所决定。 他认为，物体对加速的阻力不应该是关于空间的一个粗暴事实；它应该是宇宙中其余的物质赋予它的东西。 因此，当爱因斯坦于1917年写下第一个相对论宇宙学时，他围绕一种普遍的「世界物质」来构建它——一种充满宇宙的光滑分布，相对于自身处于静止，它将提供一切运动赖以度量的标准。

paragraphs.en: And the thing is that this is an assumed symmetry that could just as well be broken in reality, for all we know. De Sitter had objected to exactly this in 1917, noting that Einstein’s construction makes time “practically absolute” and that the assumption anyway “serves no other purpose than to enable us to suppose it not to exist.” Fifteen years later, he put his name to the Einstein–de Sitter model, built squarely on it. paragraphs.zh: 问题在于，这是一种假定的对称性，就我们所知，它在现实中完全可能被打破。 德西特在1917年正是针对这一点提出了反对，他指出爱因斯坦的构造使时间“实际上变成了绝对”，而且这一假设无论如何“除了让我们能够假定它不存在之外，别无其他用途”。十五年后，他却把自己的名字署在了完全建立在这一假设之上的爱因斯坦–德西特模型上。 这说明这一假设早已根深蒂固——连它最早的公开批评者也停止了抵制——而宇宙学的标准表述从那时起就一直沿用同样的出发点。

paragraphs.en: In contrast, for my PhD I took as a starting point a universe that is essentially uniform in every direction, as our universe appears to be, and I asked what it would be like if all the matter in the universe moved along lines we typically assign to photons of light, while light gets assigned to the at-rest comoving bundle of worldlines.
paragraphs.zh: 相比之下，在我的博士研究中，我以一个在各个方向上基本均匀的宇宙作为出发点——正如我们的宇宙所呈现的那样——然后我提出这样一个问题：如果宇宙中的所有物质都沿着我们通常赋予光子的路径运动，而光却被赋予静止的共动世界线束，那么宇宙将会是什么样子。

paragraphs.en: The result of this reassignment of worldlines is a cosmological model that has the same form as a black hole, but one in which the universe must grow over time and become larger than its initial size, rather than shrinking towards an end-point. Given my focus of wanting to figure out why the universe should naturally expand as it’s observed to do, this seemed like good progress since such a universe must necessarily expand.
paragraphs.zh: 这种世界线重新分配的结果，是一个与黑洞具有相同形式的宇宙学模型，但在这个模型中，宇宙必须随时间增长并变得比其初始尺寸更大，而不是向一个终点收缩。 鉴于我一直想弄清楚为什么宇宙会像观测所显示的那样自然膨胀，这看起来是一个不错的进展，因为这样的宇宙必然要膨胀。

paragraphs.en: And in physics terms, it poses something rather intriguing: the relativistic spacetime that’s generated is not uniform because it’s all based around this bundle of worldlines that are all moving uniformly in a specific direction; however, since the model universe is uniform by definition, and since matter is all forever moving uniformly through it , at any particular moment in cosmic time a snapshot of the universe at all earlier times must still appear uniform.
paragraphs.zh: 而从物理学的角度来看，这提出了一个相当耐人寻味的问题：所产生的相对论性时空并不均匀，因为它完全围绕这束世界线构建，而这些世界线都在沿着特定方向匀速运动；然而，由于模型宇宙根据定义是均匀的，且物质永远在其中匀速运动，因此在宇宙时间的任何一个特定时刻，对宇宙在所有更早时期的快照必然仍然显得是均匀的。

paragraphs.en: You can picture this by imagining every person on Earth as running along our lines of latitude at exactly the rate the Earth spins: none of us would ever move relative to each other, and any snapshot of the Earth taken at any moment would show a constant distribution of people. If instead we described our positions relative to the surface of the Earth, we’d all be moving quickly around it at rates that depend on our distance from the poles.
paragraphs.zh: 你可以这样想象：设想地球上的每个人都沿着我们的纬线，以恰好等于地球自转速度的速率奔跑：我们彼此之间就不会有相对移动，而且在任何时刻拍摄的地球快照都会显示出人员的恒定分布。 反过来，如果我们相对于地球表面来描述自己的位置，那么我们都会以取决于我们与两极距离的速率绕着地球快速移动。

paragraphs.en: The model I constructed worked just like this. And then I made a really surprising and I think remarkably intriguing discovery: by forcing the spacetime geometry to be general relativistic (meaning that it’s required to be a solution of Einstein’s field equations), and then by working out the rate that matter (i.e. galaxies) would measure the universe to expand at, I found that the specific rate was forced by the geometry to be a simple trigonometric rate that turns out to be identical to the flat ΛCDM rate of the standard model — its matter and cosmological-constant terms; radiation does its work locally rather than setting the cosmic rate, as I show below.
paragraphs.zh: 我构建的模型正是这样运作的。 接着我有了一个非常令人惊讶、而且我认为极为引人入胜的发现：通过强制时空几何满足广义相对论（即它必须是爱因斯坦场方程的解），然后推算出物质（即星系）所测量到的宇宙膨胀速率，我发现该速率被几何强制为一个简单的三角函数速率，结果与标准模型的平坦ΛCDM速率完全相同——即其中的物质项和宇宙学常数项；而辐射如我在下文所示，是在局部发挥作用，而非决定宇宙的整体速率。

paragraphs.en: This was in the spring of 2010; taking stock:

paragraphs.en: I was very excited about the discovery, and I hastily and excitedly wrote up what I’d found. I sent it to my supervisor to read and went to his office the following morning to discuss and… he screamed at me.

paragraphs.en: I’ve recently realised that I don’t think I ever got over that moment. paragraphs.en: It was around November 2024 when I brought up the feeling I had of living in the Twilight Zone to my counsellor. It wasn’t just the lack of support from the university for a programme I’d taken from a few hundred students per year to a couple thousand, or the fact I could see a route to explaining what I still consider the most significant and the most significantly unacknowledged problem in physics. It’s things like the fact that most physicists and physics communicators seem to see no problem at all with describing spacetime as a thing that exists, mistaking the map for the territory.
paragraphs.zh: 大约在2024年11月，我向我的心理咨询师提起了一种仿佛生活在《阴阳魔界》中的感觉。 这不仅仅是因为学校对我一手从每年几百名学生的项目发展到几千名学生的项目缺乏支持，也不仅仅是因为我看到了一条路径，可以解释我至今仍认为是物理学中最重大、也最严重未被承认的问题。 还有些事情，比如大多数物理学家和物理科普工作者似乎完全看不出把时空描述成一种实际存在的东西有什么问题，这是把地图错当成了疆域本身。

paragraphs.en: It’s the fact that when I try to bring up Einstein’s collapse of clock synchrony and ontological simultaneity as a pure symmetry of our world, in spite of the fact that standard cosmology routinely breaks that symmetry but only in the most contrived way possible, people tend to call that “just philosophy.”
paragraphs.zh: 事实上，当我试图提出爱因斯坦对时钟同步性与本体论同时性的消解——将其视为我们世界的一种纯粹对称性——时，尽管标准宇宙学经常破坏这一对称性，但只是以最牵强附会的方式破坏，人们却往往把这称为“仅仅是哲学”。

paragraphs.en: It’s the fact that the standard arguments people have used to ground black hole physics for sixty years are logically invalid and no one is willing to acknowledge my reasoning and argue against it, since I’m too easy to ignore.
paragraphs.zh: 六十年来人们用来奠定黑洞物理学基础的标准论证在逻辑上是无效的，而没有人愿意正视我的推理并对其提出反驳，因为我太容易被忽视了。

paragraphs.en: But slowly, over the past couple of years, with the help of a lot of really good people I think that I have pulled through. A year ago, I managed to publish some articles with my thoughts about spacetime and black holes that were really widely read. And the feedback I’ve received gave me comfort after nearly two decades that I’m probably not insane or stupid or a shitty writer — or any of the other things you worry about when things that seem so obviously wrong are repeatedly met only with apathy, indifference, or ignorance.
paragraphs.zh: 但慢慢地，在过去几年里，在许多真正优秀的人的帮助下，我想我已经挺过来了。 一年前，我设法发表了几篇文章，阐述了我对时空和黑洞的看法，这些文章得到了非常广泛的阅读。 而我收到的反馈让我在近二十年之后感到安慰：我大概并没有疯，也不愚蠢，也不是个糟糕的写作者——也不是那些当看起来明显错误的东西一再只遭遇冷漠、无视或无知时你所担心的其他任何情况。

paragraphs.en: And finally this spring I came to a point of understanding and clarity about black holes that pointed the way towards a consistent picture of gravitational collapse and cosmogenesis. I spent the summer working through the mathematical details , fleshing out a framework that augments general relativity by fixing a cosmological symmetry-breaking, and which provides an answer to the rhyme I’d noted in my thesis, in the apparent connection between black hole geometry and this particular cosmology. The many well-known problems of the standard cosmological model are not so much resolved as dissolved within this framework; they simply never arise, and all they really cost is to break that symmetry Einstein preferred.
paragraphs.zh: 最终在今年春天，我对黑洞达到了一种理解与明晰的境地，这为引力坍缩与宇宙生成的一致图景指明了方向。 整个夏天我都在梳理数学细节，充实一个框架：它通过固定一个宇宙学对称性破缺来扩展广义相对论，并为我论文中注意到的那个呼应——黑洞几何与这一特定宇宙学之间明显的关联——提供了答案。 标准宇宙学模型的许多著名问题在这个框架中与其说是被解决，不如说是被消解了；它们根本不会出现，而这一切的代价仅仅是破坏那个爱因斯坦偏爱的对称性。

paragraphs.en: So, to answer the question I posed as the title of this piece — the one that’s been the main driver of my intellectual journey so far — I’m now reasonably assured it is this: the universe expands because it exists. Existing as it does — a three-dimensional world enduring through cosmic time, on a geometry in which the passage of that time is the growth of its size — it cannot do otherwise. Collapsed matter must continue as an expanding cosmology; the expansion is the collapse read from the other side; and the rate is fixed by the cosmological constant alone. What the rest of that universe looks like — where it came from, what crossed its beginning, and why it began to speed up when it did — will be the subject of a companion piece.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，为了回答我在本文标题中提出的问题——这个问题一直是我至今求知之旅的主要驱动力——我现在比较有把握地认为答案是：宇宙之所以膨胀，是因为它存在着。 它既然存在着——一个在宇宙学时间中延续的三维世界，其几何结构中时间的流逝即是其尺寸的增长——它就不可能有别的选择。 坍缩的物质必然延续为一个膨胀的宇宙学体系；这种膨胀是从另一侧读出的坍缩；而其速率仅由宇宙学常数决定。 那个宇宙的其余部分是什么样子——它从何而来，有什么穿过了它的起点，以及为什么它在那个时刻开始加速——将是下一篇姊妹文章的主题。

paragraphs.en: Inside a black hole, this same geometry makes shrinking inevitable. There, the passage of time is the shrinking of the radius, and nothing that exists can avoid its own tomorrow. Read from the other side, the passage of time is growth. That’s the whole answer in one picture: nothing pushes the universe outward, any more than something pushes today into tomorrow. To exist, here, is to expand.

paragraphs.en: Eddington actually floated this possibility in 1933, in a footnote to the objection I quoted above: that the system “collapsed, and is now on the rebound,” its inward velocities “turned into outward velocities by passage through the centre.” He set it aside because, as he put it, it was “not advocated by anyone.”
paragraphs.zh: 爱丁顿实际上在1933年就提出过这种可能性，在我上面引用的那条反对意见的脚注中：即该系统“已经坍缩，目前正在回弹”，其向内的速度“在穿过中心时转变为了向外的速度”。但他将这一想法搁置了，因为正如他所说，它“并未被任何人所提倡”。

paragraphs.en: Now look at the bottom panel. After the Big Bang the deceleration fades, and at the curve’s slowest point it turns into acceleration. No dark energy component is added to do that. The acceleration is the curvature of space itself on the cosmic slice of an underlying maximally symmetric substrate — a forced cosmic breaking of that maximal symmetry. The expansion decelerates while that slice is curved one way, passes through flat at the curve’s slowest point, and accelerates once it curves the other way. The whole expansion history is set by the cosmological constant and a single number, x₀, that records when we are on the curve. Fit to the most precise survey of the universe’s growth we have, the DESI collaboration’s 2025 map of thirteen distance measurements across seven kinds of galaxy, the curve fits as well as the data allow, and it places the onset of acceleration at a redshift of about 0.68, which is exactly x₀ − 1. Together with the angle the microwave background’s acoustic ripples subtend on the sky — which this cosmology computes rather than adjusts, since there is no early-universe parameter to adjust it with — those distances fix today’s expansion rate at about 68.6 kilometres per second per megaparsec. That leaves the disagreement with the locally measured rate exactly where it stands for the standard model: this cosmology neither adds to it nor removes it.

paragraphs.en: Radiation is still there, doing its work locally. The light elements are cooked as the plasma re-expands on the way out of the collapse, at the standard rate, and deuterium and helium-4 land within one standard deviation of their measured values. paragraphs.en: Not everything is finished, and I’ve included a list of the current open problems with the collection of papers. The sharpest is in the microwave background. Carried through to the sky with nothing adjusted, this cosmology’s sound peaks land where they’re measured: their spacing is right to about one part in six hundred, and the first three peaks fall where the sky puts them. What doesn’t yet line up is their relative heights — how strongly each peak rises against its neighbours. The construction is clear about where in the history that shape is set and what the calculation has to carry faithfully there, and that is the work going on now. The fluctuations’ amplitude and tilt are inherited from the collapse, the way the standard model inherits its baryon ratio, and dark matter’s identity isn’t something the geometry answers.

paragraphs.en: Daryl Janzen is an astronomer, physicist and philosopher based at the University of Saskatchewan, where he teaches astronomy and researches the foundations of cosmology and time. His work challenges dominant space-time paradigms and proposes a new framework—Cosmological Relativity—for understanding the universe’s evolving structure.
paragraphs.zh: 达里尔·扬森是一位天文学家、物理学家和哲学家，任职于萨斯喀彻温大学，他在那里教授天文学，并研究宇宙学与时间的基础问题。 他的工作挑战了主流的时空范式，并提出了一种理解宇宙演化结构的新框架——宇宙学相对论。
